newsitem.title: POLAND: World Bank may help finance Polish pension reform.
newsitem.headline: World Bank may help finance Polish pension reform.

text.p: The World Bank is ready to help finance the reform of Poland's inefficient social security system, the restructuring of the mining sector and motorway construction, the bank's representative said on Wednesday.

Paul Knotter told Reuters the bank could give Poland an adjustment credit to cover the large costs of moving away from the current pay-as-you-go obligatory social security premiums to private pension funds.
"We are ready to cover part of those costs," Knotter said without elaborating.
"We will not promote a single solution (of how the reform should be done). Our task is to present to the Polish government an array of solutions in various parts of the world," he said.

Knotter added the World Bank had declared it could credit the programme of motorway construction, but the government said it preferred credit guarantees for loans from banks, as it believed it could find commercial financing of the project.
Knotter said the bank's offer to help in the restructuring of the ineffective mining sector has so far not been seriously discussed.
He said the bank had prepared a plan of financing municipal ventures in small Polish towns and that at the beginning of 1998 it would open a $200 million credit line for the modernisation of roads.
